stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, summarizing 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 6 (Cartier on the St. Lawrence) and Princeton Review Chapter 6 (French fur trade and Native alliances).
stimulus.text: From the early 1500s, French fishermen and traders along the North Atlantic coast exchanged iron tools and cloth for furs with Native peoples. Jacques Cartier explored the St. Lawrence River in the 1530s and found Native peoples already trading furs. The fur trade depended on Native hunters and trappers, so French traders built partnerships with Native nations instead of large settler colonies, mines, or missions.

stem: In the 1500s, French activity in North America centered on trade with Native peoples rather than mines, missions, and large settler populations. Which of the following best evaluates this difference from Spain?

options.misconception: France possessed capable ocean-going ships; technology did not prevent French conquest elsewhere.
options.text: France lacked the naval technology needed for transatlantic conquest
The fur trade depended on Native hunters, so cooperation served French interests better than conquest

options.misconception: The French also used coercion; no such blanket legal prohibition shaped their colonial model.
options.text: French royal decrees strictly forbidding the enslavement or coercion of Native peoples anywhere in the North American colonies

options.misconception: France lacked major silver colonies; the fur trade was its American economic base.
options.text: France had already secured enough silver from its other colonies

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
